evidence.reason: The polling loop checks its deadline only between iterations, but both `inspect` (line 56) and `logs` (line 61) are invoked without any timeout derived from the remaining budget. A slow or hung subprocess can therefore outlive the deadline before the loop can return the budget stop or reach the cleanup in `finally`, so the existing wall-clock bound is not actually enforced. This is an implementation defect in the current intended behavior, not a new requirement.
